fullText:
DUBAI/WASHINGTON, Sept 20 (Reuters) - Iran and the United States exchanged new threats on Sunday, with President Donald Trump warning Iran would fail economically or face its leadership being wiped out if it didn't make a deal, and the Iranian ‌military saying it would retaliate harshly to any fresh attack.

The conflict has looked stalemated for months, with no sign either side was ready ‌for concessions even as it has deepened a global energy crisis, cratered swathes of Iran's economy and spilled over into new regional escalations.

In a phone call with a Fox News reporter, Trump ​said Iran's leaders should make a deal, rot economically or be wiped out, the reporter said.

However, with Iran's President Masoud Pezeshkian expected in New York this week for the United Nations General Assembly, Trump said he would be open to meeting him, the Fox reporter added.

Trump has repeatedly made vague threats of major military escalations during the conflict that began with US and Israeli strikes on February 28, without carrying them out.

Earlier, Iran's military central command said any new attack would trigger sustained ‌retaliation against US bases and interests and that Washington's ⁠regional allies would be considered parties to the conflict.

The Iranian military added that it had information that an attack was being prepared, without elaborating on what that information might be.

US Gulf allies have already been badly scarred by a ⁠war that the US and Israel launched with no warning, bringing their cities under Iranian fire and hammering their economies with the crucial Strait of Hormuz waterway blockaded.

On Saturday their predicament worsened further, with Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi group launching missile and drone strikes at the Saudi capital after having made sudden military gains in Yemen's reignited civil war ​earlier ​this month.

The US State Department ‌issued a security alert citing the Houthi hostilities. It said there was potential for unforeseen escalation in the Middle East, and Americans should exercise more vigilance and be aware of possible flight cancellations and airspace closures.

Saudi Arabia did not comment on the incident, though a Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said it had foiled other attacks on the kingdom.

Recent escalation by the Houthis has forced Riyadh into a painful dilemma: continue airstrikes on the group to stop it seizing more Yemeni territory or step back in the hopes of averting drone strikes on critical infrastructure.

The Houthi gains along the coast mean the group's forces ‌now sit on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, giving them easier control over shipping travelling between ​the Red Sea and Asia and the ability to blockade the crucial waterway.

With Iran already ​having blockaded most shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, the oil-rich Gulf's ​energy exports are now almost entirely cut off from global markets, adding to pressure on oil prices.

A US blockade of ‌Iranian ports is meanwhile stopping Iran from selling its own oil, ​contributing to major problems in the Islamic ​Republic's economy.

Despite the economic damage, there is little sign of a return to the interim ceasefire agreement that was struck in June but fell apart in July amid disputes over its terms.

Iran reiterated on Sunday that it would not reopen the Strait of Hormuz until the terms ​of that June agreement, as it interpreted them, were met.

Iranian ‌Parliament Speaker Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf said Iran would have to keep on fighting as well as negotiating, to push back its enemies ​and to consolidate any gains with diplomacy.

title: What have we learned from the Premier League so far?
description: BBC Sport takes a look at the opening weeks of the Premier League season as a long international break arrives.
fullText:
The Premier League takes a near three-week break as we enter a four-game international window.

So, what have we learned from the opening five matches of the season?

Premier League champions Arsenal were looking fairly unstoppable in the opening weeks of the season.

A win over Brighton on Saturday would have given the Gunners a club-record equalling eighth consecutive win in all competitions to start the season.

But that all ended with a 3-0 loss at Amex Stadium on Saturday.

The Gunners had not lost a league game by more than one goal, let alone three, since October 2024.

It was their heaviest defeat in the league since May 2023 when they lost 3-0 to the same opposition.

"That's not going to take away what the team has done and the boys have done in the last six or seven weeks since coming back from the World Cup," said boss Mikel Arteta.

"What we've done, the way we've competed and the amount of games we've won has been remarkable - but this is a big lesson for all of us to understand what it takes to win at this level."

Brighton humbling 'a big lesson' for Arsenal - Arteta

Many wondered if Manchester City would experience a post-Pep Guardiola slump when the legendary boss left after a decade.

Things did not start too well under Enzo Maresca, with the Community Shield defeat by Arsenal.

But they have won all five games in the Premier League - and seven in a row in all competitions - after Sunday's entertaining 5-3 win over Sunderland.

That takes them three points clear of Arsenal.

"In the press conference before the game, I said I expect a very tough game," said Maresca. "Then we also conceded two or three goals but we have learned a lot in these eight weeks and this is good."

Perfect 24 hours as Man City put pressure on Arsenal

Brighton and Brentford, two clubs who have never won a major trophy, have continued to impress this season.

Fabian Hurzeler's Brighton enjoyed that 3-0 win over Arsenal to see them sit third in the table, only two points behind the Gunners.

Brighton have won at home against the reigning Premier League champions in each of the last three seasons.

Star player Pascal Gross laughed and said "no" when BBC Sport asked him if Albion were in the title race.

But stranger things have happened...

Meanwhile, just one point below them in the table are Keith Andrews' Brentford.

Many tipped the Bees to struggle after the departure of Thomas Frank last summer but if anything they improved under their former set-piece coach Andrews.

And their start to this season - unbeaten after five games and fourth in the table - is showing he is no one-season wonder as a manager.

They go into the break on the back of their most impressive result, a 3-0 home win over Chelsea.

Leeds, impressing again under boss Daniel Farke, are also on nine points and in a potential Champions League place.

Andoni Iraola's Liverpool and Everton are just below them on goal difference.

From near oblivion to Europe - Brighton celebrate 125th anniversary in style

Seven years apart, United did the same thing twice hoping for different results - appointing a club legend who last managed in Britain in the Championship after a good start as caretaker boss.

In 2019 it was Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and this time it was Michael Carrick.

But this season, after Carrick having a summer to work on his team, the Red Devils have only won once in the league.

Their five points after five league games is their joint fewest at this stage of a Premier League season.

They go into the international break on the back of a 1-1 draw against Fulham, and even needed a late deflected Matheus Cunha strike to stop the Cottagers winning their first game all season.

After the Lisandro Martinez own goal that give Fulham the lead, ex-United captain Gary Neville said on Sky Sports: "I've watched Manchester United since the age of five and that's the worst 15 minutes I've ever seen.

"Absolutely pathetic. I've never seen such a lack of effort."

United's owners will have almost three weeks to stew on this before they host fellow underachievers Tottenham (more on them soon) on 10 October.

In 2024 and 2025, the three promoted teams went straight back down - mostly with really low points tallies too.

But that streak came to an end last year when Sunderland finished seventh to qualify for Europe and Leeds came 14th. Only Burnley went down.

And the early weeks of this season indicate we could be in for a similar situation.

Hull City are eighth after five games, with their 2-1 loss to Newcastle their first defeat.

Ipswich are 11th. And Coventry, after losing the first four games without scoring, beat Nottingham Forest 1-0 and only sit in the drop zone on goal difference.

A Coventry win 25 years in the making

Tottenham finished 17th the last two seasons, their lowest two finishes since being in the second tier in 1977-78.

But expectations were raised after a summer of big spending - with Spurs splashing out £302m as well as making two high-profile loan signings.

Defence and midfield in particular were overhauled, with new wingers too.

But they are left with one senior striker in Dominic Solanke, who has only scored 12 Premier League goals in over two years at the club.

"I feel they have overpaid for every player they bought this summer - you can't rule them out from being in and around the relegation battle," said TNT pundit and ex-England international Joe Cole.

Saturday's 3-2 loss against Aston Villa sees them sit 19th going into the break - despite scoring their first two league goals of the campaign.

"We have to put on the pitch something more than we are putting," said manager Roberto de Zerbi.

"Football is tactical but it is blood, it is fighting, it is first one on the ball. We will suffer until the next game."

No revival in sight for 'fragile' Spurs after Villa defeat

Many were keen to see what Xabi Alonso could do at Chelsea this season.

The Spaniard memorably led Bayer Leverkusen to a historic unbeaten German double in 2023-24.

And they made big changes to their squad this summer, with £117m attacking midfielder Morgan Rogers and new first-choice keeper Emiliano Martinez both coming in from Aston Villa.

There have been 22 goals in their five league games - more coming against them than for them - and they sit 10th.

And that is not even counting the 6-3 win over Leeds in the Carabao Cup.

Hugely entertaining for the neutrals - but perhaps not for Chelsea fans or management.

title: Liverpool have signed one of the best in the world, he's incredible

fullText:
Liverpool have an incredible player who could win the Ballon d'Or very soon.

In the history of the Reds, there's only been one Ballon d'Or winner. There should have been more. Mo Salah and Virgil van Dijk have definitely made a case for it in the past.

But they existed in a world where Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo were superhuman. They were impossible to stop from winning those Ballon d'Ors, they were simply in a league of their own.

So, that means Liverpool's only Ballon d'Or winner to date is Michael Owen. Yes, Michael Owen. Not Steven Gerrard, not Kenny Dalglish or Ian Rush but Owen.

A player whose legacy at Anfield is very much tarnished by the way he left for Real Madrid and then joined Manchester United.

The era of Ronaldo and Messi is coming to an end now though. Both of them are fizzling out of the elite level and there's a new generation looking to win their fair share of the accolades.

Kylian Mbappe is probably at the forefront. He will be one of the favourites to win the award this year. Harry Kane will be another.

After Rodri and Ousmane Dembele having won the award, the Ballon d'Or is certainly a lot more attainable for anyone.

Liverpool have an exciting new generation who will be motivated to play a role and leave their legacy on the modern game.

Among those players will be the likes of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola. But there's another who if he keeps going will win the Ballon d'Or.

In the history of the award, there haven't been many centre-backs to have won the accolade.

It's an achievement reserved for the very best. Fabio Cannavaro won it after Italy won the World Cup. And while Rodri wasn't a centre-back, winning the award as a holding midfielder after Spain won the Euros is also a notable achievement.

The key denominator here is that first and foremost you have to be one of the best in the world, and you have to experience tournament success.

Jacquet already ticks one of those boxes. Based on his form, the Reds have signed one of the best defenders on the planet.

The fact that he plays for France, who are likely to be successful at the Euros and the World Cups in the future means if he keeps going the way he is, he will win a Ballon d'Or, it's simply inevitable.

title: Juventus 2 – Atalanta 0: Initial reaction and random observations
description: Juventus went into the first international break of the season with their second win in the span of four days, beating the always-tricky Atalanta in the process.
fullText:
Following last Sunday's last-second loss to Sassuolo, Juventus had 180 minutes to try and get back on track a little bit before the first international break of the season arrived. It involved two very different kinds of opponents — a struggling Dutch side and a domestic opponent that Juve had barely had any success against at the Allianz Stadium over the past decade.

Thursday night saw the first Europa League fixture passed with flying colors, the kind of one-sided scoreline on the scoreboard in Europe that we haven't seen from Juventus much at all in the past few decades.

And what about Sunday's return to Serie A?

Well, it wasn't a 5-0 win like against NEC Nijmegen, but it was a return to winning ways domestically.

Thanks to a second half in which Atalanta rarely looked all that dangerous, Juventus were able to put La Dea away with a towering Gleison Bremer header and claim a 2-0 victory at the Allianz Stadium. It marked Juventus' first home victory over Atalanta since the pre-COVID days of 2018 — something that both speaks to how the Boys from Bergamo had previously risen to be a constant thorn in the Bianconeri's side but also how the current state of the club is far from where it was seven or eight years ago.

We can say the same about Juventus, of course. See what we saw last weekend against Sassuolo is reminder of just how far off the 2018 version they currently are.

But on this day, with the opposing manager being the last man to lift the Scudetto in Turin, Juventus looked much, much better than the team they lined up against.

There was no stretched defense for much of the second half. There was no worrying when the hammer would fall because Juventus' game state was just all over the damn place. As compared to seven days earlier, how Luciano Spalletti's squad closed out the game was a breath of fresh and the hope is that it continues once this lengthy international break actually comes to a close during the second weekend of October. (Yes, it's that long of a break.)

Things weren't great for Juventus in the first half. That's even after Francisco Conceição gave them the lead in the 28th minute. Juve recorded all of three shots total against the team that entered Sunday's game allowing the most shots per game in Serie A so far this season. Things looked OK, but nothing to be overly excited about.

The second half, though, that was a change for the better. A much-needed change for the better to see out the win, too.

Was it the change at the half to bring on Pape Matar Sarr and have a little more steel and running in the midfield? Was it the fact that it looked like Maurizio Sarri didn't change much of anything at the half? Or maybe it was just simply Juventus playing better than they did in the opening 45 minutes?

Either way, Juve really did control the second half in a way that we couldn't say about the way things went to begin the game.

You combine this with the win over NEC midweek and it's the kind of response you were hoping to see from Juventus following the loss to Sassuolo. That doesn't mean that everything is all good now and there's no reason to worry anymore. There's still a host of injuries to important players, with many of them being long-term absences. There are much tougher opponents on the schedule before the second international break of the season arrives and those same players are back from injury.

But when you consider the immediate future, Spalletti and Juventus did well to get through the first steps of the difficult moment. They got two wins when they needed to and now go into the break with a little less heat on them as compared to where things stood seven days earlier.

Thankfully that's the case because seeing Juventus lose a second straight Serie A fixture would have been brutal for a club that is already dealing with long-term injuries up and down the roster with no immediate respite in sight. Now we just hope that Juventus players don't go out and then come back from international duty with the same kinds of injuries we've seen from previous international breaks.

It sure was nice to hear Allianz Stadium singing in the way they were at the end of that game. Feels like it's been a while since we've heard that strong of a voice from the supporters. (Not like they've had a ton to be happy about the last couple of years, but we know they are a driving force in a lot of ways.)

Ah, yes … Mauruzio Sarri going with an Atalanta midfield three of players who have all been linked with moves to Juventus within the last couple of years. Instead, they all ended up in Bergamo.

This Atalanta … not like the Atalanta of a couple of years ago, folks.

Is that because they no longer have Teun Koopmeiners? (Don't answer that. Let the joke sit.)

In all seriousness, though, Koopmeiners was perfectly OK as Juve saw the win out. He did his job.

More importantly, another signing by Cristiano Giuntoli — you know, the guy who is now in charge of building Atalanta's roster — continues to look pretty good for Juventus. That would be Douglas Luiz. That decision by Spalletti to keep him around this summer is looking better and better by the week.

And we're getting Douglas Luiz sombreros in the closing minutes of a Juve win now? My goodness.

Dad was at the stadium! Everybody look at how good Dad looks!

That man is a couple of months away from being 52 years old and looks fantastic. It's not just because of the beard that he continues to roll (incredibly well), either.

How many different positions did Weston McKennie play in this game? Because I lost track. I seriously did.

Sure like when Bremer plays like this as compared to whatever it was he was doing against Sassuolo. This Bremer is a lot better than that version. And the proof was in just how strong Juve were defensively on top of his scoring the goal that put Atalanta away.

While Randal Kolo Muani didn't score a goal on Sunday, this sure felt like the kind of game we could get used to seeing from him. Should he have scored? Yeah, maybe. But it was everything else that he did that was an encouraging sign that he may be starting to seriously get out of his struggles from the first couple of weeks of the season. My man was active — and a lot of the good things Juve did in attack went through him. More of this, Randal, because the goals will follow it this kind of performance becomes a regular thing.

Seriously, some of the one-touch passing sequences that Kolo Muani was involved in were just lovely.

Thankfully Juventus were up 2-0 in the final minutes because the visual of Nick Woltemade basically running toward three or four Atalanta defenders on the counter with nobody else in bianconero around him was amusing. It's different if it's a 0-0 game, of course.

Woltemade is just German for giraffe. At least that's what I think it means.

Guglielmo Vicario had to make one save in this game. It was a good one.

But that doesn't mean Vicario was just a total spectator against Atalanta. He had plenty of his patrolling of his penalty area to do. And he did it well — which pretty much had me thinking about how Juve's last starting goalkeeper probably wouldn't have done it as well as Vic did. For that, I am thankful.

Starting to really like what Pape Sarr brings to Juventus' midfield. More of that after the international break.

Zeki Celik good. And now we're getting assists? Not bad for a guy who hasn't played much on the left.

You know who is also good? Jhon Lucumí. That man defended his ass off against Atalanta.

I would like if the version of Pierre Kalulu from last season showed up again. He has not been that good in both phases of the game so far this season. His crossing has been off. Same can be said for his defending. And let's just not discuss the risk he ran with the pulling of a player's jersey in the box from the first half. A different day and a different referee and that could have been a PK at a point where Juve didn't need it.

This is a classic Conceição kind of game, right? As much as the goal is the highlight for him, there's also so many questionable decisions that he made that leaves you just wanting more.

Edon Zhegrova with an assist after his two-goal game against Sassuolo last weekend. Not bad.

This Sunday was better than last Sunday. I feel like that is not a very controversial opinion.

That's also a pretty good way to go into an international break — especially one where the Italian papers are going to totally over-discuss certain talking points because of the extra week thrown in there despite how many games Gli Azzurri play.

So yes, we crack open the bourbon for good times this weekend. Certainly not for the reasons of last weekend. For that, I am also very thankful.

Just days after missing out on Mauricio Pochettino's latest USMNT squad for the upcoming extended international break, Christian Pulisic is back among the goals as Milan lock horns with Lecce at San Siro.

It's been a different period for the American star of late, but hope seemingly arrived in the vein of Ruben Amorim this summer, who viewed Pulisic as 'perfect for the way I think (about) football.'

But fast-forward to the present, where the 28-year-old has routinely been left out by the Portuguese tactician, Pulisic was handed a start as the Rossoneri looked to continue their undefeated start to the 2026/27 Serie A season.

He delivered when called upon in the opening half to break the deadlock against Salentini, doing well to bring down Strahinja Pavlović's ball over the top before gliding home past Wladimiro Falcone.

A first goal since December 2025 and on his first start of the season is certainly one way to, hopefully, begin to silence some of his critics as the key attacker looks to get back to his best.

title: What have we learned from the Premier League so far?
description: BBC Sport takes a look at the opening weeks of the Premier League season as a long international break arrives.
fullText:
The Premier League takes a near three-week break as we enter a four-game international window.

So, what have we learned from the opening five matches of the season?

Premier League champions Arsenal were looking fairly unstoppable in the opening weeks of the season.

A win over Brighton on Saturday would have given the Gunners a club-record equalling eighth consecutive win in all competitions to start the season.

But that all ended with a 3-0 loss at Amex Stadium on Saturday.

The Gunners had not lost a league game by more than one goal, let alone three, since October 2024.

It was their heaviest defeat in the league since May 2023 when they lost 3-0 to the same opposition.

"That's not going to take away what the team has done and the boys have done in the last six or seven weeks since coming back from the World Cup," said boss Mikel Arteta.

"What we've done, the way we've competed and the amount of games we've won has been remarkable - but this is a big lesson for all of us to understand what it takes to win at this level."

Brighton humbling 'a big lesson' for Arsenal - Arteta

Many wondered if Manchester City would experience a post-Pep Guardiola slump when the legendary boss left after a decade.

Things did not start too well under Enzo Maresca, with the Community Shield defeat by Arsenal.

But they have won all five games in the Premier League - and seven in a row in all competitions - after Sunday's entertaining 5-3 win over Sunderland.

That takes them three points clear of Arsenal.

"In the press conference before the game, I said I expect a very tough game," said Maresca. "Then we also conceded two or three goals but we have learned a lot in these eight weeks and this is good."

Perfect 24 hours as Man City put pressure on Arsenal

Brighton and Brentford, two clubs who have never won a major trophy, have continued to impress this season.

Fabian Hurzeler's Brighton enjoyed that 3-0 win over Arsenal to see them sit third in the table, only two points behind the Gunners.

Brighton have won at home against the reigning Premier League champions in each of the last three seasons.

Star player Pascal Gross laughed and said "no" when BBC Sport asked him if Albion were in the title race.

But stranger things have happened...

Meanwhile, just one point below them in the table are Keith Andrews' Brentford.

Many tipped the Bees to struggle after the departure of Thomas Frank last summer but if anything they improved under their former set-piece coach Andrews.

And their start to this season - unbeaten after five games and fourth in the table - is showing he is no one-season wonder as a manager.

They go into the break on the back of their most impressive result, a 3-0 home win over Chelsea.

Leeds, impressing again under boss Daniel Farke, are also on nine points and in a potential Champions League place.

Andoni Iraola's Liverpool and Everton are just below them on goal difference.

From near oblivion to Europe - Brighton celebrate 125th anniversary in style

Seven years apart, United did the same thing twice hoping for different results - appointing a club legend who last managed in Britain in the Championship after a good start as caretaker boss.

In 2019 it was Ole Gunnar Solskjaer and this time it was Michael Carrick.

But this season, after Carrick having a summer to work on his team, the Red Devils have only won once in the league.

Their five points after five league games is their joint fewest at this stage of a Premier League season.

They go into the international break on the back of a 1-1 draw against Fulham, and even needed a late deflected Matheus Cunha strike to stop the Cottagers winning their first game all season.

After the Lisandro Martinez own goal that give Fulham the lead, ex-United captain Gary Neville said on Sky Sports: "I've watched Manchester United since the age of five and that's the worst 15 minutes I've ever seen.

"Absolutely pathetic. I've never seen such a lack of effort."

United's owners will have almost three weeks to stew on this before they host fellow underachievers Tottenham (more on them soon) on 10 October.

In 2024 and 2025, the three promoted teams went straight back down - mostly with really low points tallies too.

But that streak came to an end last year when Sunderland finished seventh to qualify for Europe and Leeds came 14th. Only Burnley went down.

And the early weeks of this season indicate we could be in for a similar situation.

Hull City are eighth after five games, with their 2-1 loss to Newcastle their first defeat.

Ipswich are 11th. And Coventry, after losing the first four games without scoring, beat Nottingham Forest 1-0 and only sit in the drop zone on goal difference.

A Coventry win 25 years in the making

Tottenham finished 17th the last two seasons, their lowest two finishes since being in the second tier in 1977-78.

But expectations were raised after a summer of big spending - with Spurs splashing out £302m as well as making two high-profile loan signings.

Defence and midfield in particular were overhauled, with new wingers too.

But they are left with one senior striker in Dominic Solanke, who has only scored 12 Premier League goals in over two years at the club.

"I feel they have overpaid for every player they bought this summer - you can't rule them out from being in and around the relegation battle," said TNT pundit and ex-England international Joe Cole.

Saturday's 3-2 loss against Aston Villa sees them sit 19th going into the break - despite scoring their first two league goals of the campaign.

"We have to put on the pitch something more than we are putting," said manager Roberto de Zerbi.

"Football is tactical but it is blood, it is fighting, it is first one on the ball. We will suffer until the next game."

No revival in sight for 'fragile' Spurs after Villa defeat

Many were keen to see what Xabi Alonso could do at Chelsea this season.

The Spaniard memorably led Bayer Leverkusen to a historic unbeaten German double in 2023-24.

And they made big changes to their squad this summer, with £117m attacking midfielder Morgan Rogers and new first-choice keeper Emiliano Martinez both coming in from Aston Villa.

There have been 22 goals in their five league games - more coming against them than for them - and they sit 10th.

And that is not even counting the 6-3 win over Leeds in the Carabao Cup.

Hugely entertaining for the neutrals - but perhaps not for Chelsea fans or management.

title: USA loss a game Ireland 'should have won' - Bemand
description: Ireland head coach Scott Bemand says their defeat against USA in the WXV Global Series opener at Tallaght Stadium was "a game we should have won".
fullText:
Ireland head coach Scott Bemand said their defeat against USA in the WXV Global Series opener at Tallaght Stadium was "a game we should have won".

USA, led by County Dublin-born head coach Jack Hanratty, fought back from trailing 31-12 at one stage of the second half to score four successive tries and claim a 40-36 comeback win.

A loss of discipline in the second half contributed to Ireland's loss after their impressive first-half display, and Bemand was frustrated that they let the game slip out of their control.

"We came out of the blocks, moved the ball well and got momentum and showed our style of play. USA then got some momentum using their power game and we've got to be a bit cuter and smarter in stopping teams getting that momentum," he told TG4.

"When teams get momentum the penalty count is more likely go up. There's bits we can control, not from a discipline perspective but in terms of our technical process, how we can be faster finishing tackles and getting break down pressure."

USA stun Ireland with comeback WXV win in Dublin

A late try from Dorothy Wall as the clock ticked into red gave Ireland the chance to snatch a late win, but they were unable to add another with their last attack of the game as USA turned the ball over.

While pleased with the resilience shown from his side to keep fighting to the end, Bemand was disappointed that they were forced to scramble for a late winner having cruised through long periods of the game.

"You never expect our girls to give up but it's a shame we put ourselves in that position," he added.

"It's a game, I'm not saying we would have ever romped home on the scoreboard, but I think we'll look at it and think it's a game we should have won.

"How we rally at the end, you don't want to find yourselves in a position to do that."

Next up for Ireland is two games against Japan, one in the WXV in Galway next weekend and another in Cork at the start of October, and Bemand is hoping for a strong response.

"Every time we have issued a challenge to our players they've responded. We need to get 80-minute performances, having a good 40 minutes isn't what we're about," he added.

"It's two more opportunities to show what we can play like. [I'm] really excited with how we can take our learnings today and go and come back better."

title: GB's Backstedt wins world time-trial silver
description: Britain's Zoe Backstedt, 21, wins silver in the women's time trial and Belgium's Remco Evenepoel claims a fourth men's title at the UCI World Road Championships in Montreal.
fullText:
Great Britain's Zoe Backstedt produced a superb ride to claim silver in the women's time trial at the UCI World Road Championships in Montreal.

The 21-year-old Welsh rider could have opted to defend the under-23 title she won last year.

But instead she stepped up to elite level and finished 40.11 seconds behind defending champion Marlen Reusser of Switzerland, who retained her crown on her 35th birthday with a winning time of 50 minutes 24.44 seconds.

Belgium's Remco Evenpoel, meanwhile, became the first rider to win the men's time trial for a fourth consecutive occasion.

The 26-year-old reigning Olympic champion joins Germany's Tony Martin and Swiss rider Fabian Cancellara as the only men to have won the title four times.

He finished the 39.2km course in 44:53.13, beating Italian runner-up Filippo Ganna by 57.31secs, while French 19-year-old Paul Seixas was third.

"It's amazing," said Evenepoel on creating his own piece of cycling history, adding to the world time-trial titles he won in Rwanda (2025), Switzerland (2024) and Scotland (2023).

"It was obviously the goal to come and win here for the fourth time in a row.

"It was a big motivation and I just have to thank the whole team around me for the preparation... I am super happy, it was a wonderful experience again."

Callum Thornley, the British under-23 champion, put in a promising display to finish 10th, while team-mate Ethan Hayter was 18th.

In the women's event, Backstedt started third from last and set the time to beat as she came home 5.43secs quicker than Germany's Franziska Koch, who eventually finished third.

She told reporters that she started to dream of winning after making a storming start: "In the first half, when I heard the first time check, I was thinking 'OK, maybe it's possible'.

"But I knew also that Marlen was super strong and that she has a very big engine.

"So I knew that it was possible that she would bring a lot of time back on me and she did, so massive respect to her."

Reusser, the final rider to start, was more than 10 seconds behind Backstedt at the first checkpoint but paced her effort brilliantly on the 39.2km course, which was almost double the usual length, to claim a second time-trial gold medal to add to last year's victory in Rwanda.

The Swiss star, who has also won two world silvers and a bronze in the discipline, was the form rider going into the championships.

The four-time European champion had been virtually unbeatable at the discipline this year, having won time-trial stages at the Tour de France Femmes and Giro d'Italia Women.

But Backstedt made her battle hard on a long, winding, technical course to secure just the third British medal in the discipline, with Emma Pooley taking gold in 2010 and bronze a year later.

She added: "My main thing was 'don't go out too hard, don't go out like it was a 22km time trial, go out like it was a 40km time trial and if you have got anything left in the final then give it everything that you have got'."

The Briton, a former world junior and under-23 time trial champion, won both the women's road race and time trial at this year's British Championships.

"Zoe proved today that she deserves to be up there racing with the elites," British rider Hayley Simmonds told BBC Sport.

"She really put her mark on this race. She was leading for the first two intermediate checkpoints and still finished in second.

"It's not like she went out too hard and died, she just had a very mature race and I am excited to see what she can do in the next few years."

Backstedt will ride again in the women's elite road race at the World Championships on Saturday, 26 September.

Elsewhere, reigning European road race champion Demi Vollering was eighth, while Backstedt's British team-mate Anna Morris finished 16th.

title: Perfect 24 hours for Maresca as Man City put pressure on Arsenal
description: Manchester City head into the international break in a jubilant mood after enjoying the perfect 24 hours this weekend.
fullText:
Manchester City head into the international break in a jubilant mood after enjoying the perfect 24 hours this weekend.

City saw champions Arsenal thumped 3-0 by Brighton on Saturday and they capitalised the following day by beating Sunderland 5-3 in a thriller at Etihad Stadium.

Manager Enzo Maresca said before Sunday's game this was his side's "toughest" test of the season so far, but the end result cements an ideal start to his role at City, where he faced the unenviable task of replacing Pep Guardiola in the summer.

The knives were being sharpened on Maresca after a Community Shield humbling by Mikel Arteta's Gunners in August but City have responded in superb fashion with seven straight victories in all competitions.

"To be honest, I prefer to win 1-0 than 5-3 but I expected a very difficult game," said Maresca. "I knew how they good are, off the ball very aggressive and on the ball they have different weapons, set-pieces and [Brian] Brobbey.

"I know it was a difficult game but [I'm] happy because we found a way to win the game and the good thing also is that these seven official games we played, they are all different, we experienced different things.

"In the last one with 10 men and today was a complicated one - the Bournemouth one we were losing 1-0 so also a chance to learn from the game."

Arsenal's stunning loss on the south coast opened the door for City and they took full advantage.

They are the only side in England's top four divisions with a 100% winning record intact, going three points clear at the top of the Premier League.

Such has been the brilliant start that Maresca becomes only the sixth Premier League manager to win his first five games in charge at a club after Carlo Ancelotti, Craig Shakespeare, Maurizio Sarri and Ole Gunnar Solskjaer.

The other name? Predecessor Guardiola when he took over at City in 2016.

On the pitch there were plenty of positives to take too, including the return to form of Antoine Semenyo with two goals and an assist, Rayan Cherki's delightful performance and Enzo Fernandez scoring his first goal for the club.

Meanwhile, striker Erling Haaland's late effort means the Norwegian ticked off Sunderland from his scoring list - he has now netted against all 25 Premier League teams he has faced.

It means City have put pressure on Arsenal in the early stages of the campaign, with the Gunners previously being tipped as heavy favourites to retain their crown.

City, though, will undergo a stern examination upon their return to action after the three-week international hiatus, facing a trip to unbeaten Liverpool on Sunday, 11 October.

Former Reds midfielder Charlie Adam described it as a "brilliant start to the season" for City, adding on BBC Radio 5 Live: "A lot to work on but [positive] to score five goals at home and have shown that level of performance.

"With Arsenal losing on Saturday, [City] could have gone into the break top of the table and they have done that today."

Before facing the Black Cats, City had only conceded two goals in their first four Premier League games.

On Sunday, they ended up shipping three in 90 minutes and the way the side lost control will be of some concern to Maresca.

Sunderland striker Brobbey ran captain Ruben Dias ragged all game and managed the rare feat of scoring a Premier League hat-trick and ending up on the losing side - the Dutchman becoming just the sixth player to achieve that unwanted statistic.

Regis le Bris' side could have scored more and their expected goals (xG) of 4.25 was the most by any visiting side on record at Etihad Stadium in a Premier League game.

Maresca said: "I am always concerned, always trying to see what we can do better. For sure, two of the three goals we conceded were too easy.

"The second coming from a quick [Granit] Xhaka free-kick and that cannot happen. The third goal comes from another free-kick, too easy in that way.

"We concede more chances but we scored five, created [more] and could score two or three more."

Adam said: "Maresca will be delighted in terms of how it has gone, the new players coming in and how he has adapted to being the Manchester City manager.

"In terms of things to improve on, they can't go through a season playing like that, they need to be able to control spaces at times, instead of getting dragged everywhere man against man."

He added for Marseca this will provide a "real positive feeling" and that City "can go into this international break with real pride".

title: USA stun Ireland with comeback WXV win in Dublin
description: The United States stage a remarkable second-half comeback to beat Ireland 40-36 in their WXV Global Series opener at Tallaght Stadium.
fullText:
Tries: Elmes Kinlan, Moloney-MacDonald, Wafer, Higgins, King, Wall Cons: O'Brien (3)

Tries: Perris-Redding, Rogers, Treder (2), Taufoo, Tafuna Cons: Vogel (5)

The United States staged a remarkable second-half comeback to beat Ireland 40-36 in their WXV Global Series opener at Tallaght Stadium.

Scott Bemand's side raced into a comfortable lead after 20 minutes following tries from Vicky Elmes Kinlan, Cliodhna Moloney-MacDonald and Aoife Wafer and went in 24-12 ahead at the break.

Erin King added a fifth try early in the second half as Ireland looked to be cruising at 31-12 up, but a loss of control and discipline aided USA, who under the guidance of their Irish head coach Jack Hanratty, managed to turn the game around.

Elmes Kinlan's yellow card was a turning point, with USA taking advantage of their numerical advantage as they scored four successive tries to take an unlikely win.

In the first women's rugby Test match to take place at the home of football team Shamrock Rovers, Ireland started with intent and, after persistent pressure, they made the breakthrough on seven minutes.

Bemand's side carved USA open with a slick passage of play as Moloney-MacDonald found Stacey Flood with a quick offload and she drove forward before feeding Elmes Kinlan, who finished in the corner.

Their second try arrived on 14 minutes with Moloney-MacDonald scoring off the driving maul before Wafer then forcing her way over soon after to further extend their advantage.

The Eagles, who were without Ilona Maher, responded well after that tough start and co-captain Georgie Perris-Redding got them on the scoreboard as she bundled over on 25 minutes, with teenager Bella Vogue nailing the conversion.

Ireland re-established their comfortable lead just two minutes after USA's try as Anna McGann galloped forward and offloaded to Eve Higgins to dot down, with Dannah O'Brien adding the extras.

USA came again at the other end and the experienced Hope Rogers crashed over after patient play to narrow the gap again before the break.

Ireland started the second half as did the first and added a fifth try soon after the restart.

Robyn O'Connor darted forward and Erin King eventually grounded the ball with the try awarded after a TMO (television match official) review.

Ireland then dropped off and USA capitalised with Kathryn Treder scoring after peeling off a driving maul from the line-out.

Elmes Kinlan was then sent to the sin-bin for not rolling away quickly enough from a tackle and USA punished the hosts.

Treder was again on the scoresheet with a carbon copy of her first try and USA then edged in front for the first time on 69 minutes as Hallie Taufoou forced her way over with Vogel accurate from the tee to give them a two-point lead.

With momentum on their side, the USA pressed home their advantage with Freda Tafuna scoring the pick of their tries as she held off a number of Irish players before diving over.

Dorothy Wall got a late try for Ireland as the clock ticked into red, but they were unable to add another with their last attack of the game as USA turned the ball over and held out for a fine win.

Bemand's side will now look to bounce back in their next game against Japan in Galway on 27 September.

title: Hewett & Reid star as GB win fifth World Team Cup
description: Great Britain become World Team Cup champions for the fifth time as Alfie Hewett and Gordon Reid secure a 2-1 victory over Japan in Florida.
fullText:
Great Britain became World Team Cup champions for the fifth time as Alfie Hewett and Gordon Reid joined forces to secure a 2-1 victory over Japan in Florida.

Japan were the defending champions of the competition, which is the wheelchair tennis equivalent to the Davis Cup and Billie Jean King Cup.

However, Hewett and Reid ensured Britain got their hands back on the trophy with a 6-1 6-2 win in the deciding doubles match against Tokito Oda and Daisuke Arai.

"We're really happy to get the title back," said Reid, who was also part of the World Team Cup-winning squad alongside Hewett in 2015, 2019, 2023 and 2024.

Hewett added: "It's the first time it's come down to the deciding doubles for us, so I'm just really happy that we got over the line.

"It's always a privilege to play for your country and there's been a great atmosphere and team spirit again this week between all the lads."

Reid got Britain off to a winning start on Saturday with a commanding 6-2 6-2 victory over world number 21 Arai, who he has now beaten in all five encounters between the pair.

The start of the second singles match was then delayed because of extreme heat in Orlando, with Hewett and Oda returning to court six hours later when temperatures had cooled.

Just a week after beating the world number one in the singles final of the US Open, Hewett was unable to repeat his feat as he fell to a narrow 6-4 7-5 loss.

"I'm a bit disappointed that it wasn't a 100% day after my loss in the singles, but it was a really high-level match and just came down to a few points in both sets that could have gone either way," he said.

However, Hewett bounced back in the doubles alongside Reid as Britain, who also had 21-year-old Ben Bartram in the team and were captained by Martyn Whait, backed up their wins against South Korea and the Netherlands earlier this week.

title: Ngetich breaks women-only half-marathon record
description: Kenya's Agnes Ngetich breaks the world record for a women-only half marathon as she wins gold at the World Road Running Championships in Copenhagen.
fullText:
Agnes Ngetich broke the world record for a women-only half marathon as she took gold at the World Road Running Championships in Copenhagen.

The Kenyan claimed victory in one hour, five minutes and 15 seconds as she took a second off the previous record, which her compatriot Peres Jepchirchir set in winning the World half marathon gold in 2020.

Ethiopia's Letesenbet Gidey holds the overall women's half-marathon world record with a time of 1:02:52.

"My coach believed in me and told me that I could do it, that I could win the gold medal," said Ngetich, 25. "So, I am very happy and very grateful to now hold the world half marathon record, too."

In April 2025, Ngetich set a new 10km world record when she clocked 29:27 to become the first woman to run the distance in under 30 minutes in a women-only race.

She also broke the 10km world record in Valencia in 2024, becoming the first woman to run the distance in under 29 minutes when she won a mixed road race in 28:46.

Ngetich added: "I am now going to discuss with my coach what is ahead of me. But I know I am coming back to track races in 2027, because there is a World Athletics Championships.

"It is my dream to win a gold medal on the track. It is the only one I am missing."

Sweden's Andreas Almgren won the men's half marathon as he broke his own European record by 35 seconds, crossing the line in 58:06 in Copenhagen.

Dragonfly 2.0 Delivers More Performance For This Modern Replacement To Redis & Memcached

Released on Wednesday was a new version of the Dragonfly database that continues to promote itself as "the world's most efficient in-memory data store" and a modern replacement to the likes of Redis and Memcached while being fully compatible with their APIs.
Dragonfly 2.0 saw its major version number bumped to reflect its "maturity, performance, and production readiness." With this new version there is expanded Redis and Valkey compatibility with Valkey 9 RDB loading support and other enhancements.
Performance continues to be a driving focus for the Dragonfly in-memory database with the v2.0 release now reducing connection processing and memory accounting overhead while bringing other optimizations. Buffering and RDB serialization costs are also said to be lower with Dragonfly 2.0. The new version also provides configurable burst and cool-down limits for background defragmentation, among other enhancements.
Those wishing to learn more about Dragonfly 2.0 for this in-memory data store can be found via GitHub. Dragonfly continues to be developed under the Business Source License 1.1.

title: Will the three-week break put more pressure on managers?
description: So far this season three coaches have lost their jobs, but plenty of others will be looking over their shoulders heading into the new, extended international break.
fullText:
Three weeks is a long time in football - especially if you are a manager struggling for results.

So far this season three coaches have lost their jobs - Paul Heckingbottom at Preston North End, Michael Duff at Wycombe Wanderers and Peterborough's Luke Williams.

But plenty of others will be looking over their shoulders heading into the new, extended international break.

That includes the managers of Fulham and Manchester United, who on Sunday meet at Craven Cottage in the final fixture before players jet off around the world with their countries.

It will all be pretty new to Alvaro Arbeloa, appointed as Fulham's manager in the summer after taking charge of just 28 games as Real Madrid boss in the second half of last season.

But with no wins and three defeats in his first four Premier League matches, and speculation of unrest among the squad due to players' social media activity, the pressure is already on Arbeloa.

Likewise Michael Carrick at Old Trafford, especially after the 3-2 EFL Cup exit to Brighton on Wednesday.

It was the first time United had led at home by two goals and lost since they were beaten 3-2 by Tottenham in 1976, half a century ago.

Coming on the back of the 1-0 loss to 10-man Manchester City, and with their only victories this season against Ipswich Town and Sabah, Carrick needs results.

But they are not the only managers who might have cause for concern.

Over the past 10 years, it has been rare for a Premier League manager to be replaced this early in the campaign.

Even more so in the international break.

But could it be different this year? The first break is longer, three weeks rather than two, and comes later.

The September slot used to come at the start of the month when clubs had only played three league fixtures.

In the past 10 years only two managers - Watford's Javi Gracia in 2019 and Nottingham Forest's Nuno Espirito Santo last year - moved on during this break.

What about the October stoppage? Again, only two managers have previously lost their jobs during the same period - Francesco Guidolin at Swansea in 2016, and Xisco Munoz at Watford in 2021.

This suggests clubs do not tend to use an international break to change manager.

It is, though, far more likely to happen in November, with six bosses replaced in the past 10 years.

That does not mean managers are safe, though. The changes simply were not made during the breaks.

In the past 10 campaigns, nine coaches had left their jobs by the time the second international break came along - which is where we are in the number of games.

With no manager to move on yet, could it come in the next three weeks?

Former Stoke, West Brom and Middlesbrough boss Tony Pulis explains when the pressure can build for a football manager.

With the first international break upon us, rumblings around certain clubs that have started the season poorly have surfaced.

In my time, the October/November international breaks, the pause just after the Christmas period, and then early March would be the three sticking points for any manager who was struggling with results.

Why these breaks are used for clubs to make changes is plain to see. The pause in the season gives football clubs the chance to appoint a new manager with time for them to settle into their new role, to take stock of the surroundings, staff and time to prepare for their first game in charge.

After Christmas, usually the first game is an FA Cup match, which again gives the new boss a chance close up to see what they have to work with. First impressions can be a vital starting point, so again the manager has time to prepare and deliver their principles to the lads.

Personally, I've joined quite a few of my clubs midway through seasons, and have left a few clubs going the other way, but I do honestly believe that those international breaks, for the reasons I've given, definitely heighten the chances of struggling managers getting the sack.

I don't see this September break as a flashing light, it is too early in the season, but from then on in, the dates I have mentioned really do come into play.

But this early international break doesn't help any managers.

Whether your team is winning or losing, on both accounts, it's a nightmare. If you're winning you want to keep playing, and yet if you've started badly as a manager you want more time to put it right. Players travelling and the chance of injuries at such an early stage of the season is completely bonkers in my opinion.

While the evidence suggests things have to get pretty bad for a club to change manager early in the season, a few bosses are feeling the heat.

There are ways of losing games of course, but I don't see the trip to Fulham as being 'make or break' for Carrick in the sense of his job.

Carrick says it would be "ridiculous" to think that way - and I agree.

He got enough credit in the bank last season by steering Manchester United into the Champions League to ride out a poor start to the season.

I think the issue is United generate so much debate that a loss at Craven Cottage, which would be United's first since 2009, against a team that has only one point and is bottom of the table, would lead to numerous external inquests - which in turn puts a laser focus on the club when they resume their campaign against Tottenham on 10 October.

It is unclear exactly how much danger Arbeloa is in, but there appears to be some substance to reports of disgruntlement among elements of Fulham's squad early in the campaign.

His significant tactical changes since replacing Marco Silva have left the Cottagers vulnerable at the back, although they produced a more solid display in a goalless draw away to Liverpool last weekend. Silva spent five years at Craven Cottage.

However, owner Shahid Khan has shown a ruthless streak in the past when making managerial changes. Claudio Ranieri lasted just 106 days in charge, while Felix Magath was sacked in September 2014, albeit having been appointed the previous season.

The results go from bad to worse for Tottenham. Having spent about £300m on new talent over the summer the club's owners are getting very little bang for their buck in terms of points (and goals) scored.

But there is no sense whatsoever that Roberto de Zerbi is under pressure despite the club's difficult start - no wins from five games.

The vibes with regards to how the team is starting to play are positive amid a sense that it is only a matter of time before they click.

Of course, for Tottenham, it needs to click sooner rather than later.

Pierre Sage has endured an indifferent start to life at Palace. One league win so far hasn't gone down particularly well internally, nor has the team's leaky defence since the Frenchman's arrival from Lens.

Allowances will be made for the unavailability - for a manner of reasons - of key attacking duo Ismaila Sarr and Jean-Philippe Mateta.

The 4-0 win over Lech Poznan in the Europa League on Thursday eased some of the pressure, but a defeat at Leeds this afternoon would come at the worst possible time for Sage.

Nicky Hayen quit Genk to spearhead Burnley's bid to return to the Premier League at the first attempt.

The Clarets started the season as third favourites for promotion, behind West Ham and Wolves, but are winless in their first eight matches.

In his pre-match news conference on Friday, the Belgian faced questions about his future.

Hayen admitted he was under pressure and Saturday's game against fellow slow starters Derby was a must-win fixture.

But a disappointing 1-1 draw, with the Rams scoring a stoppage-time leveller, left Burnley rock-bottom going into the break.

The Burnley board might now be assessing their options.

Derby manager John Eustace, who almost took the club to the play-offs last season, is not safe either with the club in the relegation zone.

A Watford manager can never rest easy in their seat. Alessio Dionisi, appointed in the summer, became their 27th permanent manager in just under 18 years.

Friday's defeat at Bristol City left the Hornets with two wins from their first eight league games under the Italian, who managed Empoli before moving to England.

Sitting in 19th position in the league table, three points above the drop zone, it would not be a surprise if owner Gino Pozzo decided to make an early change.

title: Littler could boycott Dutch events over booing
description: Luke Littler threatens a boycott of playing in the Netherlands after being booed and whistled at the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam.
fullText:
World champion Luke Littler has threatened to stop playing in the Netherlands after being booed and whistled at during the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam.

The referee stopped the match during his narrow win against Nathan Aspinall in the last eight on Saturday to warn the hostile crowd about its behaviour, before play resumed.

It followed Littler also being booed during his win against home favourite Danny Noppert on Friday.

Littler has faced similar treatment in Germany and has stopped playing in European Tour events in the country.

Asked if he was prepared to take a similar stance for Dutch events, the 19-year-old told Online Darts: "100%."

Littler, who is expected to play at the European Championship in Dortmund in October, added: "With the Germans, I haven't been for a long time, we will have to see in Dortmund whether it changes or stays the same.

"If the Dutch stay like this, then I'm not going to do any Euro tours over there. There's just no point in me travelling, wasting my time whilst I'm getting booed.

"I just want to play my darts, obviously sign autographs.

"The past two nights, I've done nothing, I've just walked off stage and not thanked anyone. There's no point thanking everyone when they are booing me."

Littler was also booed during a win over Rob Cross at the PDC World Championship in December.

After the match, he said: "I'm not bothered [by the booing]. Really not bothered. You guys pay for tickets and you pay for my prize so thanks for booing me."

title: Dodgers GM Sends Honest Message on Tarik Skubal Trade
description: The Los Angeles Dodgers sent the baseball world into a frenzy when they traded for Tarik Skubal, but according to Andrew Friedman, it was a move the team was hoping to avoid having to make. The post Dodgers GM Sends Honest Message on Tarik Skubal Trade appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
The Los Angeles Dodgers' quest to win their third straight World Series title is alive and well, as they have officially clinched the National League West division with eight games left on their schedule. For now, the team's main goal involves getting healthy, but even if it can't, it should still be the favorite to win it all until further notice.

At the trade deadline, the Dodgers did what they always do and went all-in by acquiring the reigning back-to-back American League Cy Young winner, Tarik Skubal, in a trade with the Detroit Tigers. It was almost expected that L.A. would be the team landing Skubal, but according to general manager Andrew Friedman, this was actually a move the team was hoping to avoid having to make.

With the Tigers failing to sign Skubal to a long-term contract extension over the offseason, he ended up being the big fish that every team wanted at the trade deadline. Of course, landing Skubal was going to require a massive haul of prospects, which is something the Dodgers always seem to have at their disposal.

Los Angeles has developed a reputation for simply being willing to go above and beyond what every other team in the majors is willing to do. Whether it involves shelling out more money for the top free agents, or giving up whatever prospects a team wants for its top player, the Dodgers are always making moves, which is why it wasn't a surprise to see them land Skubal.

Despite that aforementioned narrative continuing to swirl around the team, Los Angeles has claimed that it didn't want to have to make this sort of move this year. According to Friedman, the list of the Dodgers' trade targets started and ended with Skubal, which could help explain why they were so willing to part with several of their top prospects for a guy who is set to hit the free agent market in just a couple of months.

"We looked to do everything we could over the offseason to avoid being a buyer in July, short of a real impact-type talent," Friedman said, per Tom Verducci of Sports Illustrated. "And so, from our standpoint, our buy side list was Tarik Skubal. End of list."

Trading Skubal was always going to be risky for all 29 other teams in the majors because if he hits the open market, the Dodgers are going to be the favorite to sign him. Without a true salary cap in place, nothing is stopping Los Angeles from spending above and beyond what every other team is spending on its roster, and it has put that theory to the test over the past few years.

It's gotten to the point where a lockout feels inevitable, as the Collective Bargaining Agreement will expire at the conclusion of the season, and there has been virtually no momentum towards a new deal. For now, the Dodgers are intent on winning another championship, but their actions could wind up being at the center of a very important discussion this offseason, with many folks viewing the Skubal trade as the final nail in the coffin.

fullText:
The tech industry is struggling to make sense of President Donald Trump's surprise announcement that he is creating an artificial intelligence task force and appointing a czar to oversee the administration's approach to the technology.

Trump, in alengthy Truth Social poston Saturday morning, said he was forming the government body and would also soon name an AI czar to lead it. He offered few details, leaving members of the tech world unsure what the task force would do, who would be involved or how it would operate.

Four representatives for the sector, who were granted anonymity because they were not authorized to speak publicly, told POLITICO that the industry was not widely informed of Trump's decision prior to the Truth Social post.

"Nobody knows what the idea even is," one of the people said. Another said that feedback on the idea was not widely solicited within the industry.

The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Several of those canvassed said they view the move as a response to growing public alarm at the developing technology's potential risks. AI researchers at top AI labs in the past few weeks have issued stark warnings about the technology's power to destroy humanity, while executives including Dario Amodei, Sam Altman, Elon Musk and Demis Hassabis have called for a slowdown so its risks can be adequately addressed.

"I think that he clearly feels pressure to say something, but he's torn because he's just spent the last few days saying that the whole thing is a hoax," Adam Kovacevich, CEO of the progressive tech industry coalition Chamber of Progress, said of Trump and his prior dismissal of AI doomsday scenarios

Since the departure of David Sacks, who stepped down as the Trump administration's previous AI czar earlier this year, the White House has been "making up AI policy as it goes," Kovacevich added. "I think it's clear they've really missed the presence of an organized leader like David Sacks was."

One of the tech industry representatives said they were confused about whether the task force would be charged with formulating more AI regulations or recommending policies that would further stimulate the tech's development.

Taylor Barkley, director of federal government affairs at the industry-aligned Abundance Institute, is eyeing it as a way to solidify a light-touch government approach to the technology he says will foster innovation.

"Any AI Force or AI Czar should have one job: keep the field open so entrepreneurs at every scale can compete, free from onerous regulation," he told POLITICO. "Existing criminal and civil law can handle bad actors. New permission regimes will stifle the very activity America needs most."

Trump's post Saturday showed a clear desire to keep the industry booming: "We will not in any way hinder or stifle the Growth of this incredible Industry. Rather, we will cherish it, help it, and watch over it, as it grows!"

Trump's comparison of the new AI task force to Space Force led at least one tech industry representative to speculate that the proposal could be led by the Pentagon. "Rather than use civilian agencies to regulate it, use the Pentagon to try and dominate it," they said.

OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Meta and NVIDIA did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the proposal.

Brendan Bordelon and John Hewitt Jones contributed to this report.

fullText:
World champion Luke Littler beat Nathan Aspinall in a dramatic finale to reach the last eight of the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam.

Littler, 19, trailed 9-8 in a best-of-19 contest that had been close throughout and he held throw in the 18th leg to force a decider.

Needing to break Aspinall's throw to win, Littler started the leg with his seventh 180 of the match and checked out 58 for a match-clinching 12-darter.

The two Englishmen had been involved in a World Matchplay classic in July, when Littler threw a nine-darter in the opening leg of an 11-8 victory.

"The pace of the game suits us both, we're good friends and we bring the best out of each other," said Littler, who has a chance to complete a clean sweep of the PDC's premier events in 2026.

"I only played well in the last session [from 6-6 onwards]. In the first two sessions, I didn't feel confident but I managed to get it to 6-6 and I was very good in the third."

The world number one will meet former Premier League champion Jonny Clayton in the quarter-finals on Sunday.

Clayton beat Japan's Motomu Sakai 10-8 and is one of two Welshmen in the last eight, with Gerwyn Price also progressing courtesy of a 10-5 win against Canada's Jim Long.

England's James Wade was the other winner in Saturday's evening session, defeating Wessel Nijman of the Netherlands, and will face Price next.

Earlier on Saturday, world number two Luke Humphries lost the deciding leg of his last-16 match against Dirk van Duijvenbode.

England's Ross Smith and Northern Ireland's Josh Rock also won their last-16 ties to complete the quarter-final line-up.

description: Great Britain men's team win bronze at the Wheelchair Basketball World Championships by defeating Germany, but GB women lose out in third-place play-off.
fullText:
Great Britain men's team won bronze at the Wheelchair Basketball World Championships by defeating Germany 67-56 in the third-place play-off.

After conceding an early lead in Ottawa, GB scored twice in less than a minute and stayed in front from then on, with Gregg Warburton leading his side's scoring with 20 points.

The outcome means Britain's men have won a medal at three consecutive World Championships after taking gold and silver at the 2018 and 2022 editions.

GB women missed out on a medal as they lost 63-50 to the Netherlands in their third-place match.

Britain, captained by Sophie Carrigill, trailed after two periods but levelled the scoring at 44-44 heading into the final quarter of the match.

The Netherlands, champions in 2018 and 2022, then stepped it up and dominated the closing quarter 19-6 to secure another medal.

Fourth place is still a big improvement for GB women, who finished ninth at the 2022 edition of the tournament.

title: New Zealand cruise to victory over Scotland in WXV

Scotland suffered a second successive defeat in the WXV Global Series as New Zealand ran out comfortable winners at Hive Stadium.

The Black Ferns ran in 10 tries while the Scots struggled to contain the number two ranked team in the world.

New Zealand took no time at all to exert their dominance, punching holes in the Scottish defence before powerful prop Mo'omo'oga Palu blasted through to score.

The Black Ferns set a tempo the Scots could just not live with, and another foray into the Scottish 22 resulted in a neat finish from lock Maama Mo'onia Vaipulu for the second try.

The visitors reasserted their authority with tries from Justine McGregor and Elinor-Plum King, but the Scots showed some guts to fashion another close-range try for Gallagher to keep them in the game at 24-14.

However, their defensive frailties were exposed as Layla Sae and Amy Du Plessis struck with superb tries to effectively end the game as a contest before half-time.

It bore many of the hallmarks of last weekend's defeat by Canada, with the Scots conceding immediately any time they looked to have found a way back into the match.

The visitors put their foot on the gas after the break with substitute Amarante Sititi and Tara Turner going over before Sae added her second try, New Zealand's ninth.

To their credit, the Scots kept the Black Ferns scoreless from the 47th minute until the final play when Alena Saili crossed for New Zealand's 10th try to round off a dominant display.

title: England crush Sri Lanka to top T20 world rankings
description: England steamroller Sri Lanka in the third T20 to complete a 3-0 series clean sweep and return to number one in the world rankings.
fullText:
Third T20 international, Old Trafford

Sri Lanka 124 all out (18.5 overs): Nissanka 36 (24), K Mendis 35 (28); Baker 2-17, Archer 2-23, Jacks 2-31

England 126-2 (9.4 overs): Buttler 62* (32), Brook 33 (21)

England won by eight wickets, won series 3-0

England steamrollered Sri Lanka in the third T20 to complete a 3-0 series clean sweep and return to number one in the world rankings.

Watched by new Test coach Stephen Fleming, England once again outclassed the tourists to conclude a one-sided series played on the fringe of autumn.

England's pace bowlers were outstanding in dismissing Sri Lanka for a paltry 124, then the home side chased the target in 9.4 overs.

Jamie Overton conceded only 15 runs in his four overs, including taking a wicket. Sonny Baker's improvement continued with 2-17 and Jofra Archer recovered from an expensive start to return 2-23.

England's fielding was sharp, best demonstrated by Liam Dawson's direct hit to run out Eshan Malinga.

The target was never likely to pose a challenge to an England batting line-up that remains powerful despite Phil Salt and Jacob Bethell being absent injured.

Though opener Aneurin Donald was out for 13, Jos Buttler and Harry Brook strolled the pursuit with a second-wicket stand of 85.

Brook was run out for 33, leaving Buttler to wrap it up with a six that left him unbeaten on 61.

The victory by eight wickets was concluded with 62 balls to spare - the most for England in a home T20 international.

The success was England's 23rd win in 26 completed T20s since Brook took charge in the summer of 2024. They have reclaimed their number one ranking from India.

The pity for this group is a rare lengthy wait until the next global T20 tournament. The next men's T20 World Cup is not until 2028, the same year T20 cricket makes its debut in the Olympics.

England are instead building towards a 50-over World Cup in southern Africa in the autumn of 2027. Three one-day internationals against the Sri Lankans begin in Durham on Tuesday.

Buttler crunches 62 not out as England seal 3-0 series win - as it happened

A feature of England's success in this format has been captain Brook's heavy use of spin bowling. On this occasion the spinners took a backseat – Adil Rashid and Dawson sent down only four overs between them.

Instead, it was the seamers to the fore, even without the variations of Sam Curran, another England player absent injured.

Baker endured difficult debuts in all three international formats, yet in this series has started to show his potential.

After Archer's first over went for 15, Baker had Lahiru Udara sky to wicketkeeper Buttler. He later returned to wrap up the innings, taking the final wicket when Dilshan Madushanka skied to Brook.

Archer was a spectator for some time after his initial struggle. When he returned, he got the dangerous Kamindu Mendis to pull to deep mid-wicket for 35.

Archer's second wicket was curious – Wanindu Hasaranga out hit-wicket attempting a slog, his bat almost placed on top of the bails.

Overton was the pick, returning his most economical figures when bowling his full allocation of four in a T20 international.

Though Tom Banton dropped a catch slipping on the greasy outfield, England's fielding was otherwise exceptional.

Brook took a sharp catch at mid-wicket to remove Pathum Nissanka for 36, Rashid was alert enough to run out Charith Asalanka and Dawson's direct hit was the coup de grace.

At the age of 29, Donald has been given an international opportunity in this series as a replacement for Salt.

He has shown only glimpses of his excellent domestic form, returning a high score of 21. On this occasion, he tried to wallop the spin of Tharindu Rathnayake over long-on and was stumped by a distance.

In Buttler and Brook, the captains past and present, England have two men in supreme form. Buttler is England's best white-ball batter of all-time, while Brook is on the way to being one of their greats.

Such is their quality, the second-wicket pair turned the remainder of the chase into little more than a glorified net.

Sri Lanka were scruffy – they conceded 17 runs in wides. The hapless nature of the visitors' display was epitomised when Brook should have been caught off Madushanka, only for keeper Kamil Mishara and point fielder Nissanka to look at each other as the ball dropped to the ground.

There was no need for Brook to attempt a single that Hasaranga fielded in his follow-through, the bowler hitting direct with a throw at the non-striker's end.

title: 'Greater things to come' says Mitchell after England winning run ends
description: Head coach John Mitchell says England's thrilling draw with Canada will inspire "greater things to come" from the world champions despite the result ending their record-breaking winning streak.
fullText:
Head coach John Mitchell believes England's thrilling draw with Canada will inspire "greater things to come" from the world champions despite the result ending their record-breaking winning streak.

England had won their past 39 Tests before Saturday's fixture.

Canada, who had lost their 13 previous meetings with the Red Roses on English soil, held England to a 26-26 draw in a nail-biting, physical battle at Exeter's Sandy Park.

It was only the second game domestically or internationally for England's players this season and, for Mitchell, one result is not justification to tear up the playbook.

Instead, he views it as a building block towards future success.

"It was just a matter of scoring across the white line," Mitchell said. "We were applying huge pressure. We just didn't convert."

Avoiding defeat means the Red Roses have extended their unbeaten run to 40 matches, a record they will hope to extend with WXV Global Series games against New Zealand, two more fixtures against Canada and another against the United States still to come.

Mitchell said: "There was such good stuff in there. I'm very patient because we're just starting and we're still alive in this Test series.

"I'm a realist. There will be greater things come as a result of this. There's a greater purpose and one Test match is not going to take us away from our purpose."

For the opening 10 minutes, the match followed the script of last year's World Cup final between the two sides, with Canada breaking the deadlock and England immediately hitting back.

But unlike last September, when they roared on to win 33-13, the Red Roses could not maintain control, with the two teams never separated by more than one try and England unable to convert 20 minutes of sustained pressure into the crucial score.

While acknowledging England would have to review their "game management", captain Meg Jones hailed the spectacle the two sides delivered.

"It was definitely tit for tat and definitely a game of momentum swinging," said centre Jones. "It was two good teams going at each other.

"It was an amazing contest and competitive as we imagined. This is the first Test. We get another two shots at it [against Canada]."

Echoing Jones' defiance before October trips to Toronto and Ottawa, Mitchell added: "We're in a Test series. It's 1-1. That's it."

England's 39-game winning run started under former head coach Simon Middleton, who, after the World Cup final defeat in 2022, led the Red Roses to a Women's Six Nations Grand Slam in 2023.

Mitchell then took charge midway through the 2023 WXV1 campaign and had won every game until this one.

England beat Scotland in the World Cup quarter-finals last September to claim their 31st straight Test win, surpassing their own record winning streak across both men's and women's international rugby union, which was set in 2022.

World Cup glory, another Women's Six Nations title and victory over Australia last weekend extended that record further.

"It's not necessarily something we speak about as a group; it's something that's just been there," Jones said of the winning run.

"We're very process-driven, so the outcome tends to look after itself."
